title: Lifting Accessories
summary: Rigging equipment must be inspected before each shift and during use, marked with safe working loads, and never loaded past those limits. Defective gear comes out of service right away.
talking_points: Inspect rigging equipment before each shift and during use. Remove defective equipment from service immediately.
Rigging must have permanent, legible manufacturer markings showing safe working loads. Never load it beyond those limits.

Chain slings need permanent markings for size, grade, and rated capacity. Job or shop hooks and links, and makeshift fasteners made from bolts or rods, are prohibited. Inspect them at least annually and remove them when wear limits in Table H-1 are exceeded.

Wire rope: do not exceed rated capacity. Remove slings with broken wires exceeding 10 percent of the total wires in any 8-diameter length. Do not shock load, and do not pull slings out from under loads.
Fiber rope: remove for abnormal wear, broken fibers, or discoloration. Rope can be used from -20 F to +180 F without load reduction.
Synthetic webbing must be marked with the maker's name, rated capacities, and material type. Remove it if it is burnt, torn, or has broken stitches.
Keep nylon webbing away from acids. Keep polyester and polypropylene webbing away from caustics.
Shackles and hooks must not exceed rated capacities. Hooks with no manufacturer recommendations must be proof-tested to twice the intended safe working load.
site_hazards_to_check: Missing or unreadable safe working load markings
Broken wires in wire rope slings, or worn chain past the wear limits
Burnt or torn webbing, or broken stitches
Makeshift hooks, links, or fasteners made from bolts or rods
Slings exposed to acids, caustics, or heat above the limits
Knots in wire rope, or slings being pulled out from under loads
discussion_questions: Where is the safe working load on this sling, and can you read it?
What would make you take a sling out of service today?
Why must we avoid shock loading and pulling wire rope slings out from under loads?
